title: an orphan, a merchant, a man who was trusted before he was believed
hookLine: an orphan, a merchant, a man who was trusted before he was believed
last: ZAKAT — WHAT YOU GIVE PURIFIES WHAT YOU KEEP.

lines: A WHOLE CITY TRUSTED ONE MAN.
cards: Who holds the spare key to your home? Probably not the most impressive person you know. The most trustworthy one, the one who has never once let you down.
The early biographies say a whole city felt that way about one man. Clans who'd fight over a camel all agreed on him, and gave him a nickname for it.
Years later, many of those same people refused to believe what he told them, and still left their valuables in his care. Today, told the way Islam tells him: in words only.

teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, peace be upon him. In Muslim tradition he isn't drawn or pictured; he's known through words, so words are all we'll use. The early biographies say he was born in Mecca, around the year 570.
His father died before he was born, his mother when he was six, and the grandfather who took him in two years later. His uncle Abu Talib raised him after that.
So when the Qur'an speaks to him, it can say: “Did He not find thee an orphan and protect (thee)?” He grew up herding sheep, then traveled with the trade caravans.

A merchant and widow named Khadijah hired him to lead hers, and was so struck by his honesty that she proposed marriage. By then Mecca had a name for him: al-Amin, the trustworthy. The biographies tell a story about it.
The clans were rebuilding the Ka'ba and nearly came to blows over who would set the sacred Black Stone back in its place. They agreed to let the next man through the gate decide. It was him.
He spread out a cloak, set the stone on it, and had a man from each clan lift a corner, together. At forty, he began to receive the Qur'an.
A saying records how he stood on a hill and asked his people: if I told you an army was behind this hill, would you believe me?

teach.h: WE'VE NEVER KNOWN YOU TO LIE.
teach.b: We've never known you to lie, they said. Then he told them his message, and many turned away. Trusted first.

how: Muslims say "peace be upon him" (or write ﷺ) after the Prophet's name, never picture him, and learn his life, the sira, from the Qur'an, the hadith and the early biographies.

games.q: what's inside his early life — tap the pairs.
p: the merchant who hired him, then married him
every clan lifted the Black Stone

s: the Prophet grew up in a wealthy, protected home
his father died before his birth, his mother when he was six, his grandfather two years later.
Mecca called him the trustworthy before his prophethood
al-Amin: the name came first, the Qur'an at forty.
the early biographies say she was so struck by his honesty that she proposed.

games.q: the clans of Mecca are about to fight over who sets the Black Stone back in the Ka'ba. you're the one asked to decide. what do you do?
o: spread a cloak so every clan lifts it together.
set it yourself and tell them to accept it.
games.why: he spread a cloak, set the stone on it, and had a man from each clan lift a corner. then he placed it himself.

practice: Think of someone who trusts you with something. A secret, a key, a child, a job. Picture them handing it over, and notice what it feels like to be trusted.
Then think of one small promise you've made lately and haven't kept yet. Nothing dramatic: a call, a book to return, a message you said you'd send. Just hold it.
If you pray, you can ask for help keeping it.

wordCard.voice: The Prophet, peace be upon him. An orphan, a shepherd, a merchant, called al-Amin, the trustworthy, long before most believed him. Twentieth word.

orig.note: Arabic: the trustworthy, the Prophet's name in Mecca before his prophethood, from the root of amana, trust.

carryVoice: Your line: al-Amin, the trustworthy. He was trusted first, and believed by many only later. Day twenty.
